chapter: Sam Morgan and the Morgan bands
title: Old bandstands, Carparelli's Hall and Young Tuxedo losing Oriel Fusche
summary: He explains how bandstands changed when pianos were added and how Oriel Fusche left the Young Tuxedo band for Sam Morgan's.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah, you see, the old-time bandstand, of course, the Carparelli's Hall is the, I don't know, they didn't knock that down. Yeah, the Carparelli's Hall, that's to be on Liberty Street. That used to be another famous hall, but now the Sandus Cinders had a piano on their bandstand. You see, now you can line up a band, when the Sandus Cinders, the piano beat mostly to the back wall, then you put your drummer there, and you put your banjo on that side. Most likely banjo player had to be almost like on the left side of the piano player, you see. And then your horns would be in the front. So when the band went to eight pieces, well that's where a fellow by the name of Oriel Fusche, he left our band, the Young Tuxedo, and went into the Sam Morgan band, which he don't blame me, because they had more work. Our band, this was coming up, taking Carparelli after the original Tuxedo band. You see, that's where around 19, between 24 and 25, 27, all like that.
